issues.description: Tense mismatch in the model sentence: the past-time clause 'After I joined the gym' is paired with a present-simple main clause 'my body feels good every week'. A native speaker would notice this wobble (natural options are 'Since I joined..., my body has felt...' or a past+past frame). It also clashes with the grammar note's past+past model ('Before I joined the gym, I sat a lot'), so as the lesson's only 'after' example it teaches a shaky pattern.
issues.suggested_fix: Change to: 'I sat a lot. After I joined the gym, my body started to feel good every week.' (keeps the after-clause, the meaning, and the review words 'body' and 'week').

issues.description: The hook 'Anna asks him about before and after' is elliptical and unnatural; a native speaker would not say 'asks him about before and after' without a noun.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the hook to: 'Ben goes to the gym now. Anna asks him about his life before and after the gym.'

qa_report.summary: A clean, level-appropriate micro-dialogue: both lines are simple A2 English, the target word 'gym' and review words 'week' and 'body' all appear, the glosses are accurate and simpler than the words they explain, and the 'before' clause is modelled well. One fix is needed: Ben's 'after' sentence mixes a past-time clause with a present-simple main clause, which is a noticeable tense wobble and undermines the grammar point it is meant to model; aligning it to a past+past frame fixes it. The hook's 'asks him about before and after' is a minor unnatural ellipsis worth tidying. Approve once the s1l2 edit is made.
